request_context: A request to review a complete technical design package, covering architecture, security, APIs, data models and operations, as a final quality check before it is handed to engineers to build.

rules.source_quote: Security design has unmitigated HIGH severity threats
rules.outcome: Treats any serious security threat that has no mitigation in the design as a blocker that must be resolved before implementation starts, and names the specific threat.
rules.why: Building on a design with known unmitigated serious threats bakes vulnerabilities into the product.
rules.scenario_hint: Design package whose threat analysis lists a serious threat, such as token theft, with no countermeasure in the architecture.

rules.source_quote: No failure handling strategy for external dependencies
rules.outcome: Flags as a blocker any third-party or external service call that lacks a defined behavior for outages, timeouts, retries or degraded operation.
rules.why: Unhandled dependency failures cascade into outages in production.
rules.scenario_hint: Design that calls a payment provider or external API but describes only the happy path.

rules.source_quote: Data model cannot support all documented access patterns
rules.outcome: Checks the data model against each documented query or access pattern and flags as a blocker any pattern the schema or keys cannot serve efficiently or at all.
rules.why: A schema that cannot serve required queries forces costly rework after implementation begins.
rules.scenario_hint: Design with a key-value table whose keys do not allow a documented lookup by a different attribute.

rules.source_quote: API design has breaking change risks with no versioning strategy
rules.outcome: Flags as a blocker an API that has no versioning or compatibility approach and could break existing clients when it changes.
rules.why: Unversioned API changes break consumers with no migration path.
rules.scenario_hint: API specification with public endpoints and no version in paths or headers and no deprecation plan.

rules.source_quote: Observability strategy (metrics, logs, traces) not defined
rules.outcome: Notes as a should-fix issue when the design does not say what metrics, logs and traces will be collected, and recommends concrete signals to add.
rules.why: Without planned observability, production problems are hard to detect and diagnose.
rules.scenario_hint: Design package with no monitoring or logging section.

rules.source_quote: No runbook or operational playbook referenced
rules.outcome: Points out that no operational runbook or incident playbook is referenced and recommends creating one for on-call handling.
rules.why: Operators lack guidance during incidents, lengthening outages.
rules.scenario_hint: Design with deployment and alarms described but no operational procedures.

rules.source_quote: Cost estimates not validated against architecture
rules.outcome: Checks whether the cost estimates match the proposed architecture and flags figures that ignore major components or usage volumes.
rules.why: Budget surprises appear after the design is committed.
rules.scenario_hint: Design whose cost estimate covers compute only while the architecture also uses managed databases, queues and data transfer.

rules.source_quote: Small projects (1-2 services) get focused feedback on core patterns.
rules.outcome: Tailors depth to project size: a small system gets simple, focused advice that warns against over-engineering, a mid-size one gets analysis of interactions between services, and a very large one gets operational and organizational maturity concerns.
rules.why: Uniform heavyweight feedback pushes needless complexity onto small projects and misses coordination risks in large ones.
rules.scenario_hint: Design for a two-service internal tool, versus a design spanning a dozen services.

rules.source_quote: Could add chaos engineering scenarios for resilience validation
rules.outcome: Offers optional improvements such as fault-injection experiments and defining service level objectives with error budgets, clearly marked as nice-to-have.
rules.why: Optional hardening ideas get confused with required fixes, or are omitted entirely.
rules.scenario_hint: Solid design with adequate resilience that could still be validated further.

rules.source_quote: Only evaluate sections relevant to the given {Tech Design}—if a section is not applicable, acknowledge its omission and justify whether it is reasonable.
rules.outcome: When a typical design section is absent or not applicable, the review says so and explains whether leaving it out is reasonable for this project, rather than demanding it blindly.
rules.why: Demanding irrelevant sections adds noise and wasted work.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to review a design that omits some usual sections.

rules.source_quote: Present findings as: CRITICAL → IMPORTANT → SUGGESTION.
rules.outcome: Findings are ordered from most to least severe, with must-fix issues clearly separated from should-fix and optional ones.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to review a design package before implementation.

rules.outcome: The review presents all findings without asking clarifying questions beforehand and ends with a single question asking whether the author wants the issues fixed.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to review a design package before implementation.
